security_spec.violation_condition: Kernel code (KVM emulation, ptrace, signal delivery, or context-switch save/restore) assumes that a single aligned memory instruction always produces exactly one memory operation for accesses wider than XLEN bits (e.g., vector V extension loads/stores), when the spec now explicitly carves out that ISA extensions may generate multiple memory operations per instruction.
security_spec.summary: Generalized RVWMO single-memory-operation guarantee now applies only to accesses of XLEN bits or fewer, with an explicit escape hatch for extensions like V to generate multiple memory operations per instruction — kernel code emulating or intercepting vector memory accesses (KVM, ptrace, signal frames) must not assume single-copy atomicity for wider accesses

findings.finding: Context-switch vector save uses vse8.v to bulk-save all 32 vector registers to a kernel-allocated datap buffer. It saves the vstart CSR too, so partially-completed vector memory operations are properly tracked across context switches. No assumption that a single vector instruction equals a single memory operation — only the register file is saved/restored.
findings.snippet:
vsetvli %0, x0, e8, m8, ta, ma
	vse8.v v0, (%1)
	add %1, %1, %0
	vse8.v v8, (%1)
	...

findings.finding: Context-switch vector restore uses vle8.v to bulk-load all 32 vector registers from a kernel datap buffer. CSR state (vstart, vtype, vl, vcsr) is restored via __vstate_csr_restore before the register reload, preserving partial-execution state for restartable vector instructions. Compliant with multi-memory-operation model.
findings.snippet:
vsetvli %0, x0, e8, m8, ta, ma
	vle8.v v0, (%1)
	add %1, %1, %0
	vle8.v v8, (%1)
	...

findings.finding: Context-switch handler correctly distinguishes user-mode and kernel-mode vector contexts. Saves dirty user vstate and defers restore (lazy restore via TIF_RISCV_V_DEFER_RESTORE). For kernel-mode vector, handles preemption flags (RISCV_PREEMPT_V_DIRTY/NEED_RESTORE/IN_SCHEDULE). No assumption of single memory operation per instruction.

KVM MMIO load emulation only decodes scalar load instructions (LW/LD/LB/LBU/LH/LHU and C variants). Vector memory instructions (vle/vlse/vluxei etc.) are not decoded and fall through to return -EOPNOTSUPP at line 450. This is a safe failure — KVM refuses to emulate rather than incorrectly assuming single-memory-operation semantics for vector instructions.

KVM MMIO store emulation only decodes scalar store instructions (SW/SD/SB/SH and C variants). Vector store instructions (vse/vss/vsoxei etc.) are not decoded and fall through to return -EOPNOTSUPP at line 567. Same safe-failure pattern as the load path.

Guest vector state save on VCPU put correctly checks SR_VS==DIRTY before saving. Uses __kvm_riscv_vector_save which delegates to __riscv_v_vstate_save — bulk register file save, no per-instruction memory-operation assumptions.
Guest vector state restore on VCPU load correctly checks SR_VS!=OFF before restore. Bulk register file restore — compliant with multi-memory-operation model.

VCPU load sequence: host_vector_save then guest_vector_restore. The vector save/restore pair swaps the register file between host and guest contexts using kernel buffers. No assumptions about guest vector memory instruction atomicity.
VCPU put sequence: guest_vector_save then host_vector_restore. Mirrors the load path correctly. Compliant.

Signal frame save copies the vector register file (via riscv_v_vstate_save then __copy_to_user) plus CSR metadata (vstart/vl/vtype/vcsr/vlenb). This is a state snapshot, not a trace of individual memory operations. Properly uses get/put_cpu_vector_context to serialize with kernel-mode vector usage.

Signal frame restore calls riscv_v_vstate_set_restore (lazy restore) then copies CSR metadata and full vector register content from the user's signal frame via copy_from_user (not __copy_from_user — correctly does access_ok check to prevent kernel info leak). Restartable vector instruction state (vstart) is properly preserved in the signaled-to frame.

Ptrace get of vector registers: saves dirty vector state (if target==current) via get/put_cpu_vector_context, then membuf_writes the CSR header and full register file. No assumption of single memory operation per instruction — this transfers the register file, not a trace of guest memory operations.

Ptrace set of vector registers: validates CSR values via invalid_ptrace_v_csr (checks vlenb match, reserved bits, vtype SEW/LMUL constraints per RVV 1.0 spec 3.4.2, VLMAX bounds), then copies CSR metadata and full register file from userspace. The validation prevents injection of invalid partial-execution state. Compliant.

Lazy vector restore on return-to-userspace: if TIF_RISCV_V_DEFER_RESTORE is set, clears the flag and calls riscv_v_vstate_restore to reload the full vector register file plus CSRs (vstart/vl/vtype/vcsr) from the kernel buffer. Called with irqs disabled. This is a bulk register file restore, not an assumption about single memory operations.

Kernel-mode vector context start: transfers ownership from user to kernel, saving user vstate if dirty. Handles nested contexts (depth tracking). The save/restore is of the register file — the vstart CSR tracks partial vector memory instruction progress. Compliant.
